Who likes robots?

“Hands up if you like robots! Wow!” Then (→) introduce yourself. Ask: “Maybe you already know: what is a robot?” Take 2 or 3 answers. Praise every one.

Say

“A robot has 3 superpowers.” (→) “It MOVES by itself, like me now.” Walk across the stage. (→) “It SENSES things. If I get close to this table, I see it, so I stop!” Walk to the table and stop. (→) “It FOLLOWS instructions, like you on your way to school every morning.”

Do

Act out every one. The kids copy you: walk on the spot, hand over eyes, salute.
🎮 Game · Robot or not?
🏃Moves by itself✓
👀Senses things✓
📋Follows instructions✓

How to play

Show the thing. Ask: “Is this a robot? Shout YES or NO!” Press Y or N for what MOST kids shouted. The answer pops up with a happy or a sad sound. → shows the next one.

If you brought real things

Hold them up at the same time: toy car, LEGO car with no motor, C104, drone.

Last card

“Are YOU a robot?” You move, you sense and you follow instructions… but you can THINK and FEEL too. That makes you even better: a HUMAN!

Say

“You are a bit like a robot every morning! First… (→) you wake up. (→) Brush your teeth. (→) Eat breakfast. (→) Go to school: turn left, turn right, until you get there. (→) Robots follow steps too. We call them INSTRUCTIONS.”

Do

Kids mime every step with you: stretch, brush, munch, walk on the spot.

Game: Human Robot!

🤖

You can ONLY do EXACTLY what I say. Nothing more!

Do

(→) Pick one child and invite them to the front. Don’t ask “who wants to?”, just choose. The computer says “Robot mode on!” in a robot voice.

Say

“You are now a ROBOT. Robots only do EXACTLY what they’re told. Ready, robot?” Teach a robot voice: “BEEP. READY.”
Round 1 · I give the orders 📣

How to play

Click a card. It fills the screen and the computer reads it in a robot voice. The robot child does it. Click or press Esc to close.

The trick: “Go over THERE!” (pink card)

Say it without pointing. The robot gets confused: ERROR! Then: “Did you see? I said ‘go over there’, but I didn’t say WHERE. When instructions aren’t clear, robots don’t know what to do!” Give the helper a big clap.

Why did the robot get confused?

😵‍💫

Not clear

“Go over there!”
Where? How far? Which way?
😎

Clear!

⬆️step⬆️step↪️right⬆️step
One small step at a time
Robots need clear instructions!

Say

(→) “When I said ‘go over there’, the robot didn’t know WHERE.” (→) “But if I say: step, step, turn right, step… the robot knows EXACTLY what to do! Robots need CLEAR instructions, one small step at a time.”
Round 2 · Now YOU are the boss! 👑
🎯Mission: program the robot (me!) to walk to your teacher and give a HIGH-FIVE 🖐️
Tap the blocks below to build the robot’s program…
Robot blocks

How to play

Swap roles: now YOU are the robot and a new child is the programmer. The child tells you (or taps) one block at a time and builds the program in the row. Press ▶ Run. Each block lights up, the computer reads it out, and you do it, robot-style.

Make it fun

Count the steps with the kids before you start. If the program is wrong, walk into the wall (gently) and say “BUG! 🐞”. Then: “Let’s fix the bug!” Undo and try again. Finding and fixing mistakes is what real programmers do.

You just spoke robot language!

→ ⬆️step↪️right👏clap =

Say

“Robots don’t understand our words like ‘go over there’. You just turned words into blocks: step, turn, clap. That’s ROBOT LANGUAGE. We call it CODE. People who write code are PROGRAMMERS. You were programmers just now!”
(→) “Future Builders learn 4 languages: talking with each other, reading, writing… and talking to tech!” (→) “In our club we build LEGO robots and give them orders with blocks on a tablet. When I SEE blue, MOVE!”
🎮 Everyone stand up!

✋Stop!Freeze like a statue
🚶Go!March on the spot
🦘Jump!Jump up high

Say

“Our LEGO robots have a COLOUR SENSOR: an eye that sees colours. When the robot sees a colour, it follows its instruction. Now YOU are robots with colour sensors! Everybody stand up!” Practise each colour once.

How to play

Press ▶ Start. Colours flash on their own and get faster. → skips to the next colour. Click or press Esc to stop. Finish on RED: “Freeze… and sit down, robots!”
Click or Esc to stop · → next colour
🎮 Game · Who can do it?

🤖Robot

Me🧒

How to play

Read the card. Kids answer with their bodies: robot arms = Robot, point at yourself = Me, both = do both! Press R, H or B for what most kids did. The card flies to its side. → shows the next card.

Key moment

The last card is “Build a robot”. Only humans build robots, so that means YOU!

So what’s the difference?

🧠

Humans think

Robots don’t think. They only follow instructions.

❤️

Humans feel

A robot can show a sad face, but it doesn’t really feel sad.

🛠️

Humans build robots

Robots don’t build humans. People like YOU build robots!

Say

(→) “Humans can THINK. Robots don’t think, they follow instructions.” (→) “Humans can FEEL. Can a robot feel sad? No! It can show a sad face because we programmed it to, but it has no feelings.” (→) “And who builds robots? HUMANS! Robots don’t build humans.”

Only YOU can…

friends

family
Robots, tablets and games are fun. But they can’t be your best friend.
Real life is better: playing outside and laughing together!

Say

“Robots are smart machines that help people. But there is one thing a robot can never do… be HUMAN! Only you can…” (→ each) think, feel, laugh, play with friends, hug your family. Kids act each one: thinking face, heart hands, laugh, kick a ball, hug yourself.
(→) “Robots, phones, tablets, games… they’re fun. But they aren’t real life. Real life is playing outside and laughing with your friends!”
